summary: Otelo Saraiva de Carvalho (1936–2021) was the officer who drew up the operational plan of the 25 April 1974 coup, having served in Angola and Guinea, and who then commanded COPCON, the operational command created in July 1974 that policed the revolutionary period. He became the emblem of its most radical wing, and lost his command after 25 November 1975. He stood twice for president, in 1976 and 1980, and in the 1980s was tried and convicted in connection with the FP-25 armed group — a conviction later annulled. He is in the atlas as the actor at the centre of both the coup and the confrontation that ended the period the coup opened.
